w: Once the city's principal thoroughfare for traffic, the Cours Mirabeau has since been closed to cars, handing its long stretch back to pedestrians. It remains Aix-en-Provence's central spine, the street every walk through the old town seems to circle back to.
_facts: Main avenue and boulevard of Aix-en-Provence
Now closed to through traffic, prioritising pedestrian access

w: Set back at 32 rue Celony, this historic pavilion is fronted by a formal French garden, one of the quieter corners of central Aix-en-Provence. It's the kind of address you stumble on rather than seek out -- a garden pavilion doing exactly what garden pavilions are for.
s: A historic pavilion behind a formal French garden
_facts: Historic pavilion at 32 rue Celony, Aix-en-Provence
Surrounded by a French formal garden

w: Built in the newer Sextius-Mirabeau district, this performance venue takes its design cue from the Montagne Sainte-Victoire, the limestone ridge that defines the Aix region -- its exterior set with stones of different colors recalling the mountain's striated face.
s: A theatre clad in stone the color of a mountain
_facts: Performance venue in the Sextius Mirabeau district of Aix-en-Provence
Exterior design references the Montagne Sainte-Victoire, using stones of different colours

w: Paul Cezanne used this studio from 1902 until his death in 1906, and it now operates as a biographical museum devoted to the painter -- the working room where some of his final canvases took shape, preserved in Aix-en-Provence for anyone tracing his life back to its source.
s: Cezanne's studio, exactly as he left it
_facts: Paul Cezanne's studio from 1902 until his death in 1906
Now a biographical museum about the painter in Aix-en-Provence

w: Opened in 1966 and renamed the Archives nationales d'outre-mer in 1987, this branch of France's national archives documents the colonial empire, with files on Algeria, French Equatorial Africa and Indochina. Half the history of France overseas, one scholar said, sits in this paper.
s: France's colonial paper trail, filed in Aix
_facts: Branch of the Archives Nationales documenting the French colonial empire
Opened 1966 as Depot des Archives d'Outre-Mer, renamed Archives nationales d'outre-mer in 1987
Holdings include records on Algeria, French Equatorial Africa and French Indochina

w: This museum in Aix-en-Provence is dedicated wholly to the work of Victor Vasarely, an entire building given over to one artist's vision. No detour needed to find a second collection here -- the whole place is a single-minded monument to Vasarely's eye.
s: A museum given over entirely to Victor Vasarely
_facts: Museum in Aix-en-Provence dedicated to the works of Victor Vasarely
